## Round 70: the placement rule is stated in the builder's own ordering comment

Blocker 1 from round 69 is now located at its source. `StatefulTransactionBuilder` (around 7141) documents the input
order it builds, and the comment is the rule the covenant violates:

```js
// Add master UTXO as first input, then data NFT UTXOs, then read-only NFTs,
// then outState NFTs, then external call NFTs, then low-level call NFTs,
// then entry NFTs, then token container UTXOs, then satoshi container UTXO
const entryInputs = this.entryNfts.filter((e) => e.exists && e.utxo)
  .sort((a, b) => a.slotIndex - b.slotIndex).map((e) => e.utxo!);
...
this.allInputs = this._buildInputs(
  entryInputs, tokenContainerInputs, satoshiContainerInputs,
  externalOutStateInputs, externalCallInputs, lowLevelCallInputs,
);
```

So participant (external-call) inputs are placed **before** the caller's own entry inputs - exactly the collision the
covenant reports:

* the covenant addresses the caller's OWN block slots as `masterInputIndex + blockLayout slot offset`
  (`output[activeInputIndex + 2]` in the measured fixture; `master + 4` for the marketplace `pay` probe), i.e. it
  assumes the caller's own block is dense from the master;
* `__internal__externalCallInputBase` is computed on the SDK side as
  `1 + requiredNftIndices.length + externalReadUtxos.length + outStateInputCount + blockhashSlots + iterationEntryInputs.length`,
  which counts the master and its data NFTs but **not** the caller's entry slots - so the participant band starts at
  the caller's first entry slot offset. For `pay` that is 4 = its `entry` slot offset, and the probe showed a callee
  input sitting there;
* functions whose writes touch only data-NFT slots are unaffected, which is why
  `unicrow params > set unicrow contract addresses` (address state vars = data NFTs, offset 1..k, plus an external
  call) passes while every mapping-write-plus-call case fails.

### Fix direction (one change, both frames)

Move the caller's own entry inputs (and, on the output side, its entry/event/trailing outputs) **before** the
external-call and low-level-call bands, in the documented order and in `_buildInputs`, then let
`externalCallInputBase` include the caller's own entry count. The output side mirrors it: the same builder
immediately below computes `externalOutputStart = 1 + requiredNftIndices.length + externalReadUtxos.length
+ externalOutStateUtxoGroups… + iterationEntryInputs.length` and inserts the participant output band there
(`externalGroupOutputCount`, used by the return-base arithmetic), so both `externalOutputStart` and the documented
input order have to change together or the output frame stays interleaved while the input frame becomes dense.

Expect fallout in every base derived from these orders (`externalCallInputBase`, `externalOutputStart`,
`delegateReturnOutputBase`, `returnEventOutputBase`, the anchor bands), so land it with the 0.3 s fixture as the
first gate (the mapping case must reach `the converged transaction` green) and then run the marketplace ladder.

## Round 71: the deferral mechanism exists but is gated to route blocks; forcing it did not reach the branch

Implementation target located exactly. In `_buildInputs` the **position-indexed** path (7250-7360) places each
resource at its `blockLayout` slot offset - i.e. it satisfies the covenant's `master + slotOffset` addressing - and
the gap between the last readOnly resource and the first entry is filled with participants:

```js
// 7444: Fill the reserved gap (offsets between last readOnly and first entry/SC/TC)
//       with external outState and external call inputs
// 7447: A compiler-route delegate executes immediately after the complete owner block, and its own nested
//       participants follow that implementation block. ... while the generated route correctly requires
//       `externalCallInputBase == OP_INPUTINDEX + blockSize`. Reserve the owner gaps with neutral funders and
//       defer the delegate's external participants until after the implementation input band.
const deferredExternalCallInputs = this.compilerRouteDelegateBlock ? externalCallInputs : [];
const gapInputs = [ ...externalOutStateInputs, ...(this.compilerRouteDelegateBlock ? [] : externalCallInputs) ];
```

So the compiler's requirement is stated in the code: for a compiled route, **`externalCallInputBase` must equal
`OP_INPUTINDEX + blockSize`** - participants come after the caller's complete block. The builder honours that only
when `compilerRouteDelegateBlock` is set; otherwise the participants fill the owner's gaps, which for any function
whose own block is wider than its data NFTs (i.e. every mapping/entry writer) lands them on the caller's entry slot.

The branch is also skipped entirely for direct builds with external groups (guard at 7262-7266:
`this.blockLayout && this.funderUtxos.length > 0 && (!hasExternalGroups || blockhashCoSpendSlotOrdinals !== undefined
|| compilerRouteDelegateBlock || delegateEntriesAfterLowLevel)`), and its own comment says why:

## Round 75: the output frame is DERIVED from input coordinates - so the reorder must re-derive every base

The output side has no independent placement: `StatefulTransactionBuilder` (~11482) maps block layouts onto the
**input** frame and derives outputs from that map:

```js
const addLayout = (baseIndex, layout, ownerCategoryId, expectedLockForSlot) => {
  for each slot of layout:
     const index = baseIndex + slot.offset;              // an INPUT index
     const input = this.allInputs[index];
     if (input is mutable, owner category, expected lock) slots.add(index);
};
const rootIndex = this.allInputs.findIndex((input) => input.txid === this.masterUtxo.txid && ...);
addLayout(rootIndex, this.blockLayout, this.categoryId);                      // the caller's own block
for (const [groupIndex, group] of this.externalCallUtxoGroups.entries()) {
  addLayout(this.getExternalCallOutputBase(groupIndex), group.blockLayout ?? ..., group.categoryId, ...);
}
```

and `getExternalCallOutputBase(groupIdx)` (16166) returns, for any group that has a `blockLayout`, the group's
**master input** coordinate (`getExternalCallMasterInputIndex(groupIdx)`), with a dense resource-count formula only
as a fallback. So:

* the whole frame is addressed through input coordinates, i.e. the "dense frame" invariant is the design, and the
  caller's own slots must be the first `blockLayout.blockSize` inputs;
* this is why round 74's experiment - which reordered the inputs but changed none of the bases - left the check
  failing: the input order moved while `getExternalCallOutputBase`, `externalOutputStart`,
  `__internal__externalCallInputBase` and the return/anchor bases still described the old order, so the frames
  disagreed rather than both becoming dense.

### Fix recipe (single commit, gated on the 0.3 s fixture)

1. relax **both** input gates together (`!hasExternalGroups` disjunct *and* `this.funderUtxos.length > 0`; see
   round 72 for the measured values) and defer participant inputs past the caller's complete block;
2. re-derive every base from the new order in the same change: `__internal__externalCallInputBase`
   (`StatefulContract.ts` ~30583), `getExternalCallOutputBase` (16166), `getExternalCallMasterInputIndex` (16103),
   `externalOutputStart`/`externalGroupOutputCount` (`StatefulContract.ts` 28880-28903), `delegateReturnOutputBase`
   and the identity-anchor bands;
3. run the fixture first: `the converged transaction that spends the bracketing entry NFT` must go green (it is the
   skipped `it` in `test/unit/SortedMappingProofInputCoordinate.test.ts`; un-skip, run, re-skip), then the
   marketplace ladder, then re-check `unicrow params > set unicrow contract addresses` (the currently green
   external-call-plus-state-write case) for regressions.

## Round 77: `funders: 0` is CORRECT for this block, so the dense path's funder gate is over-strict

Traced where the funder pool comes from. `StatefulTransactionBuilder` takes it from constructor options
(`options.funderUtxos`, 7095) and the SDK auto-funds block slots right after constructing the builder
(`StatefulContract.ts:32231`):

```js
// Auto-fund block-layout slots that need funder inputs (output-only slots like transfers/events,
// non-existing entries/TCs). These are WITHIN the block range - the covenant requires them at specific positions.
if (effectiveBlockLayout && builder.funderUtxos.length === 0) {
  const outputOnlyKinds = new Set([
    'transfer', 'tcTransfer', 'event', 'returnEvent', 'lowLevelCall', 'deploy', 'deployDataNft',
  ]);
  let neededFunders = effectiveBlockLayout.slots.filter((s) => outputOnlyKinds.has(s.kind) && ...).length;
  ...
}
```

Only **output-only** slot kinds get neutral funders, which is right: the caller's own block needs a funder input only
where it has a slot with no resource of its own. The fixture host's block is
`{master@0, dataNft@1, entry@2}` - **no output-only slots at all** - so `neededFunders` is 0, no funders are
created, and `funders: 0` is the *correct* state, not a missing pre-condition. The dense path's
`this.funderUtxos.length > 0` conjunct is therefore an over-strict proxy: for a block whose slots are all covered by
existing resources (this shape) the dense placement needs **zero** gap fillers.

That closes the loop with round 74/76: relaxing the gate is what let the dense path run, the input order became
dense, and the covenant failure disappeared - the only thing left was a 4946-sat imbalance, which must come from the
deferred band's own accounting rather than from missing gap fillers.

## Round 82: the SDK can already tell a batch-written slot - `sortedBatchInfo`

Checked the ABI metadata for the fixture's `record` (from the compiler, no test run needed):

```
entryAccesses:   [{ slotIndex: 0, collection: 'balances', keyParams: ['user'], operations: ['write'],
                    mutationEffectOrdinals: [2], valueSource: 'id:amount' }]
sortedBatchInfo: [{ collection: 'balances', slotIndices: [0] }]
```

So the distinction round 81 needs is **already published**: a slot listed in `abiFunction.sortedBatchInfo[*].slotIndices`
is written by the sorted-batch (vmap) path, which publishes its chain nodes in the trailing band
(`master + blockSize + 1 + counter`), and must therefore **not** also get a materialized fixed entry-slot output.
`entryAccesses` alone cannot distinguish it - it only says `operations: ['write']`.

`EntryNftInfo` (`StatefulTransactionBuilder.ts:6066`) carries no such flag today (`slotIndex, collection, keyType,
valueType, keyValue, keyTypes?, keyValues?, exists, utxo?`), so the suppression cannot be done from that record as it
stands; the caller that builds the entry-output list is the place to consult `sortedBatchInfo`.

### Next step (precise)

   `_buildInputs` dense branch and the `_materializeJobEventsBand`/`_reassert*` passes on `finalBuilder`), skip the
   fixed slot output for any slot in `entryAbiFunction.sortedBatchInfo[*].slotIndices`.

## Round 83: the suppression belongs in `buildEntryOutput` - the mechanism already exists

Located the exact output materialization that round 82 prescribes. `StatefulTransactionBuilder.buildEntryOutput`
(17862) decides, per entry slot, whether a slot produces an output, and it already has the gate shape needed:

```js
const buildEntryOutput = (entry: typeof sortedEntries[number]): Output | undefined => {
  if (embeddedEntrySlots.has(entry.slotIndex)) return undefined;      // <- a slot that must NOT emit an output
  if (this.entryDeletes.has(entry.slotIndex)) { ... placeholder ... }
  ...
```

and `embeddedEntrySlots` is a local `Set<number>` built in the same pass (17209, populated at 17578) for slots whose
resources are already carried by an embedded block. So the fix is to treat a **sorted-batch-written slot** the same
way: add every slot index listed in `entryAbiFunction.sortedBatchInfo[*].slotIndices` to that suppression set (or to
an equivalent set consulted at 17864), because the batch publishes its chain nodes in the trailing band
(`master + blockSize + 1 + counter`) and the fixed slot output is exactly the duplicate measured in round 81
(`out2` at the caller's entry slot, in addition to `out6`/`out7` from the batch).

Two details to preserve: the surrounding comment explains that a slot which produces no output would shift later
outputs down and desync the covenant's fixed-offset read, so any suppression must keep the *cardinality* the
covenant expects (`entryPlaceholderFillThreshold` exists for that); and the batch path's own nodes are the ones the
covenant reads in the trailing band, so they must stay.

Apply it in one commit together with the deferral (both input gates) and the base re-derivation from round 75, then

## Round 93: the value-tail registry is one-per-logical-slot, but a batch publishes two nodes

Traced how the plan's per-node commitments reach the builder:

* the SDK registers a tail with `builder.registerPendingEntryValueTail(pending)` (`StatefulContract.ts:32096`) from
  the array filled at 20272;
* the builder stores them in a `Map` keyed by **`${params.collection}|${binToHex(params.slot)}`**
  (`StatefulTransactionBuilder.ts:6961`, `set` at 15243, `get` at 15259);
* the registration happens **inside the per-slot loop over `batch.slotIndices`** (the loop that computed
  `targetCommitment` just above), so exactly one tail exists per logical slot - keyed by the key being written.

A sorted batch publishes **two** nodes: NEW at the written key and P' at its predecessor's key (measured: plan
`outputs` = [slot `0000..00`, slot `7c854a55…`], `predOutputs` = the non-target one). Only the *target* gets a
registered tail, so the predecessor node's commitment can never be derived; the assembled frame then reuses the other
node's commitment for the second output (round 92's "NEW twice") and the covenant's P' node is absent.

That is the defect behind rounds 85-92, and it is independent of the layout question: even with dense placement the
predecessor node would have no value.

### Next step

Register a tail for every batch predecessor node as well, not only per logical slot: the batch already computes them
(`predOutputs`, `batchPredCommitments`, and the per-predecessor `output.commitment` around 20240-20250 for the nested
planner), and `SortedList`/`planBatchUpsert` returns the rewritten predecessor nodes with their commitments. Key them
by the predecessor's own slot (`collection|<predSlot>`), which is what the builder's `Map` already supports. Then
re-run: the frame must publish both nodes with their own commitments (7 outputs, no 1200-sat duplicate), and the
suppression+deferral experiment can be re-evaluated on a correct value set.

## Round 94: narrowing the P'-missing defect to one of two sides (fix sketch)

Looked for how the SDK hands the batch's predecessor nodes to the builder. `batchPredCommitments` is built in the SDK
(`StatefulContract.ts:20017`, `batchPredCommitments.set(batch.collection, predOutputs.map((o) => binToHex(o.commitment)))`)
but **`StatefulTransactionBuilder` never mentions `batchPredCommitments`** (grep is empty), so the predecessor
commitments do not travel by that name into the builder. The builder's entry value path is the tail registry
(`registerPendingEntryValueTail`, keyed `collection|slot`) plus `entryNfts`.

So exactly one of two things is true, and one run decides which:

1. the predecessor node's commitment reaches the builder by some other channel (e.g. it is folded into the target's
   `entryNfts` entry or into `pendingEntryValueTails`), and the builder's *output materialization* drops it - in which
   case the fix is in `buildEntryOutput` (17862) / the legacy entry-output loop (17927/17936);
2. it never reaches the builder - in which case the fix is in the SDK, registering the predecessor node like the
   target (the builder's `Map` already supports `collection|<predSlot>`).

Fix sketch for case 2, to be placed right after the per-slot loop that fills `pendingEntryValueTails` (20260-20290):

```ts
for (const pred of predOutputs) {
  const predSlot = slotValueToBytes(bytesToSlotValue(pred.slot));
  if (list.find(predSlot) === undefined) continue;      // only nodes the batch actually rewrites
  pendingEntryValueTails.push({
    slotIndex, collection: batch.collection, slot: predSlot,
    seed: binToHex(pred.commitment), next: decodeEntryCommitment(pred.commitment).nextKey,
    chunkable: collection.chunkableValue === true,
  });
}
```

(with the caveat that a preserved predecessor's commitment is already complete, so the tail's `seed` may need to be
treated as final there - check `registerPendingEntryValueTail`'s consumer at 15243-15270 before wiring it.)

### Next step

One run: log, at the builder's tail-registry `set` (15243) and at `buildEntryOutput`'s return (with
`entry.slotIndex` and the commitment prefix), every registration and every emitted entry output while the
suppression+deferral experiment is applied. That shows whether `7c854a55…` (P') ever enters the builder; then apply
the fix on the side the run indicates, re-run, and gate on the fixture.

## Round 190: the tail registry is never used here - P' has no commitment source at all

Instrumented the builder's tail registry (`registerPendingEntryValueTail` -> `pendingEntryValueTails.set`,
`StatefulTransactionBuilder.ts:15243`) with a `value-tail-set` log and re-ran the suppression+deferral experiment with
`SOLIDC_DEBUG_VALUE_TAIL=1`. Result: **zero registrations** (the frame was the same 6-output / `out 51200` frame).

That settles round 94 in favour of case 2 and explains why: the SDK only fills `pendingEntryValueTails` in the
`resolvedWholeValue === undefined` branch (`StatefulContract.ts:20260-20290`), and the fixture's write has a
reproducible value (`valueSource: 'id:amount'`), so `targetCommitment` is computed directly by the
`encodeEntryCommitment(slot, next, valueTail)` path instead. But that computation runs **inside the loop over
`batch.slotIndices`**, i.e. once per *logical slot* - and a sorted batch publishes **two** nodes per slot. So:

* the target node (NEW) gets its commitment from that loop;
* the predecessor node (P') exists in the plan (`plan.outputs`, measured in round 92 as slot `7c854a55…` with its own
  commitment) and in `predOutputs`/`batchPredCommitments`, but `batchPredCommitments` never reaches
  `StatefulTransactionBuilder` (round 94's grep) and no tail is registered for it;
* the frame therefore has no value for P' and reuses the target's commitment for the second output, which is exactly
  the measured frame (commitment `0000..00` at both `out2` and `out5`).

So the defect is confirmed from both sides, and the fix has exactly one shape: **publish the batch's predecessor nodes
(with their plan commitments) to the builder so it materializes them as outputs**.

1. pass `batchPredCommitments` (plus each predecessor's slot/next) into `StatefulTransactionBuilder` alongside

2. materialize one output per predecessor node, using the commitments as given (a preserved predecessor's commitment

3. keep the suppression+deferral change (rounds 74/81) so the caller's own block precedes the participant band;
4. gate on the fixture: the frame must show both nodes with their own commitments (7 outputs, no 1200-sat duplicate),

## The current blocker, end to end

1. `take job`'s probe and the fixture fail at the *same* instruction, so the fixture is a faithful reproduction.
2. The covenant addresses the caller's **own** block slots as `masterInputIndex + blockLayout slot offset`
   (measured: `output[activeInputIndex + 2]`; `pay`'s entry slot offset is 4 with `externalCallInputBase == 4`).
3. Participant (external-call) blocks are placed **before** the caller's entry slots: the dense input path is gated by
   `this.blockLayout && this.funderUtxos.length > 0 && (!hasExternalGroups || …)`, and `funders: 0` is *correct* here
   (the block has no output-only slots to fill), so a mapping-writer + external call always takes the legacy order
   `master, dataNFTs, readOnly, outState, external calls, LLCs, entries…`.
4. Deferring the participants (both gates relaxed) makes the input frame dense and **removes the covenant failure
   entirely** - the send then fails only on satoshi accounting.
5. That deficit is not funding: the sorted batch plans **two** nodes with different commitments
   (`0000..00` and `7c854a55…`), the frame carries the **first one twice**, so P' is absent and exactly one node's
   satoshis (1200) are unmatched. Reusing the target's commitment is why the numbers looked like a funding gap.
6. Root cause, confirmed from both sides: `targetCommitment` is computed **inside the loop over `batch.slotIndices`**
   (one per logical slot) while a batch publishes two nodes per slot; the predecessor's commitment lives in
   `predOutputs`/`batchPredCommitments` (`StatefulContract.ts:20017`), which **never reaches**
   `StatefulTransactionBuilder` (grep is empty), and the value-tail registry is not used on this path at all
   (measured: zero `registerPendingEntryValueTail` calls, because the write has a reproducible value).

## The next change (implementation only - no diagnosis left)

1. pass the batch's predecessor nodes (slot + next + commitment from `batchPredCommitments`/`plan.outputs`) into
   `StatefulTransactionBuilder` next to `entryNfts`, and materialize one output per predecessor node with the
   commitment as given (do **not** route a preserved predecessor through the value-tail machinery);
2. keep the participant deferral (both input gates) and keep `buildEntryOutput`'s suppression of a batch slot's

## Round 198: the naive gate relaxation REGRESSES green tests - the funder conjunct is load-bearing

Applied the placement change alone (both dense-path gates relaxed + unconditional participant deferral) and ran the
one currently-green external-call case in the marketplace suite:


(Reverted; tree clean.) This corrects an over-generalisation of mine from rounds 76/85: "relaxing both gates removes
the covenant failure" was measured on the **fixture**, whose block is three slots with no gaps, and it does **not**
generalise. For a block with output-only slots (events, transfers, returnEvent) the dense path must fill those slots
with funders - which is exactly why `this.funderUtxos.length > 0` is part of the guard. Dropping it leaves the
compiler-published fixed offsets 7..16 empty and the covenant's fixed-offset reads fail.

So the ledger is now:

* the fixture's shape needs **zero** gap fillers, so the funder conjunct is over-strict *for it*;
* the general case needs fillers, so the conjunct is **load-bearing**;
* the correct change is a predicate, not a relaxation: take the dense path when every `blockLayout` slot is covered by
  an available resource **or** a funder, and make the SDK supply funders for whatever the dense path reserves. Any
  landing must therefore be validated on `unicrow params` **and** the fixture, not the fixture alone.

That is the last thing the next session needs to know before touching `_buildInputs`; everything else is in the
`START HERE` block and the close-out.

## Round 200: the slot census that pins the dense-path predicate

Read every `blockLayout` from `.marketplace/artifacts/solidcash/Unicrow.json` (static, no run). It names exactly which
functions need gap fillers and which collide with the participant band:

```
pay                 blockSize 7   master@0, dataNft@1-3, entry@4, event@5, returnEvent@6
refund              blockSize 8   master@0, dataNft@1-3, entry@4, satoshiContainer@5, transfer@6, event@7
release             blockSize 6   master@0, dataNft@1-3, entry@4, event@5
challenge/settle    blockSize 3   master@0, dataNft@1, entry@2
updateEscrowFee /
updateGovernance    blockSize 2   master@0, dataNft@1            <- no output-only slot at all
getEscrow           blockSize 3   master@0, entry@1, returnEvent@2
getAllEscrowData    blockSize 4   master@0, dataNft@1, entry@2, returnEvent@3
sendEscrowShare     blockSize 6   master@0, dataNft@1-3, satoshiContainer@4, transfer@5
splitCalculation    blockSize 2   master@0, returnEvent@1
... (unicrowArbitrator/unicrowClaim/unicrowDispute/protocolFee/governanceAddress/escrowIdCounter/
     setClaimed/escrows/__updateBlockOracle/__construct follow the same pattern)
```

Three things follow, and they are the design of the fix:

1. **`pay` needs exactly two fillers** (its `event@5` and `returnEvent@6` are output-only) and its `entry@4` is the
   slot the participant band occupies (`externalCallInputBase == 4`, measured in round 63). So for `pay` the dense
   path is *already* eligible for the funder conjunct (the SDK auto-funds `outputOnlyKinds`, `neededFunders = 2`), and
   only the `!hasExternalGroups` disjunct blocks it. That is the marketplace's real blocker.
2. **The fixture's host is the opposite case**: blockSize 3 = master/dataNft/entry with **no** output-only slot, so
   `neededFunders = 0` and the SDK creates no funders - which is why the funder conjunct blocks it while being
   load-bearing elsewhere (round 198).
3. Therefore the predicate is: take the dense path when **`neededFunders === 0 || this.funderUtxos.length > 0`**, and
   let the SDK's existing auto-funder logic fill whatever the dense path reserves. The round-198 regression
   (`missing inputs at fixed offsets 7..16`) came from taking the dense path while *also* deferring participants
   without the composed frame's trailing band being in place - so the deferral still needs the composed-order
   consistency check before landing, and the gate must be validated on `unicrow params` **and** the fixture.

With this, the next change is fully specified: the predicate above plus the predecessor-node plumbing, then re-derive
the six bases and gate on fixture -> `unicrow params` -> ladder.

Instrumented `_resolveExternalExpressionReturns`' `registeredTarget` (temporary, reverted) to print which of its
four sources matched. For the `take job` build:

```
x2  iface='IERC20'              resolved='FakeToken'         dep=True ownerReg=True  selfReg=False byName=False
```

So the callee resolution is **fine** - `IERC20` and `__raw__` both bind to the deployed `FakeToken` (via

`precomputed: undefined` for **every** group, and the probe's in-block return slot for the `transferFrom` group
(output 8, per `assigned: [[1, 8]]`) carries lock `51` with commitment `00` - the placeholder the SDK writes with
`setReturnEventOutput(categoryId, new Uint8Array([0]))`. The caller decodes that as `bool false`, which is exactly why
pay takes the inline SafeERC20 catch path.

Note also the inconsistency worth chasing in the same run: the grouping says the `transferFrom` return lives at output
**8**, while the probe's witnesses report `externalReturnOutputIdx0 = 13`, `Idx1 = 13`, `Idx2 = 7`.

## Round 206: the precompute gate explains the placeholder - and it excludes state-writing callees

`SOLIDC_DEBUG_RETURN_SNAPSHOT=1` produced **zero** `projected-return-refreshed` records for the `take job` build, so
the projection path that assigns `group.precomputedReturnCommitment` at 13301 never runs here. The two remaining
assignment sites are the nested/group loops, and both guard the precompute with the same predicate - the second is
explicit:

```js
// StatefulContract.ts:28538-28541
let precomputedReturnCommitment: Uint8Array | undefined;
if (nested.hasReturnValues && selectedFn.writesState !== true && selectedFn.outputs?.length === 1) {
  const evaluateReturn = (): Promise<FunctionArgument | undefined> => proxyCallee
    ? proxyCallee.forward(nested.functionName, childArgs).staticCall() as Promise<FunctionArgument>
    : callee._deriveReturnValue(nested.functionName, childArgs) as Promise<FunctionArgument>;
  ...
  if (value !== undefined) precomputedReturnCommitment = encodeExternalReturnValue(value, returnType, ...);
}
```

(`25946-26123` is the same shape inside the graph/nested loop.)

So **only a callee that does not write state gets a precomputed return commitment**. For pay's four calls that means:

* `IERC20.balanceOf` (x2) is a view and *should* precompute - yet the measured group table reports
  `precomputed: undefined` for it as well, so this predicate is not the whole story for the probe build and needs the
  same instrumentation;
* `__raw__` = `FakeToken.transferFrom` **writes state**, so its return is excluded from precompute by design. Its
  return event is supposed to be produced by the callee's own covenant executing in the probe
  (`returnEventInBlock` / the in-block slot at output 8 per `assigned: [[1, 8]]`), and the measured output 8 is
  lock `51` with commitment `00` - i.e. the neutral placeholder, meaning nothing executed there.

Either way the caller decodes `false` for the transferFrom success flag, which is precisely the observed failure
(inline SafeERC20 catch path at pay-body 308, message "SafeERC20 failed").

### Next step

Instrument the 28538 predicate for the pay build and print, per nested call: `nested.functionName`,
`nested.hasReturnValues`, `selectedFn.name`, `selectedFn.writesState`, `selectedFn.outputs?.length`, and whether the
`if` is entered - plus the `value`/commitment when it is. That separates the two remaining cases:

1. the predicate is entered for `balanceOf` but `_deriveReturnValue` yields `undefined` (callee probe failing), or
2. the predicate is not entered at all (so the probe is not going through this loop for a direct call, and the
   precompute belongs somewhere else).

Then the `transferFrom` half needs the probe to actually execute the state-writing callee and materialize its return
event, or the caller's success flag has to be wired independently of a precomputed commitment - the two are different
fixes and the instrumentation above will say which shape the frame is in.

```js

const fallback = physical.precomputedReturnCommitment ?? new Uint8Array([0]);
...
const parts = candidate.loopReturnCommitments?.length

```

```
  family: [ { candidateIdx: 0, fn: 'balanceOf',   parts: [ { bytes: 1, head: '00' } ] },

            { candidateIdx: 2, fn: 'balanceOf',   parts: [ { bytes: 1, head: '00' } ] } ] }
```

## Round 210: the coordinates and the witnesses are BOTH wrong, and they disagree with each other

Logged, in one `take job` run, the seed's per-event coordinate (`builder.getExternalCallReturnEventOutputIndex`)
together with the witnesses the covenant actually receives (`finalArgs` at the
`__internal__externalReturnOutputIdx*` positions) and the groups' `returnOutputIndex`:

```
groups:    balanceOf returnOutputIndex=undefined | transferFrom 8 | balanceOf undefined | setArbitrator undefined
witnesses: __internal__externalReturnOutputIdx0 = 14      <- not an output index at all (14 is the currency ANCHOR INPUT)
           __internal__externalReturnOutputIdx1 = 0
           __internal__externalReturnOutputIdx2 = 0
pendingReturns (identity, commitment, seed coordinate):
   external-call:0:0  '00'  -1      <- balanceOf #0: never placed
   external-call:1:0  '00'  13      <- transferFrom
   external-call:2:0  '00'   7      <- balanceOf #2
   external-call:2    '00'   7
```

So neither side is trustworthy today, and the disagreement is total:

* the seed places the events at **13** (transferFrom) and **7** (balanceOf #2) and leaves balanceOf #0 at **-1**;
* the witnesses say **14, 0, 0** - `Idx0` is not even an output coordinate (14 is the currency anchor *input* index from
  round 63's measurements), and `Idx1`/`Idx2` are unfilled.

The `-1` for balanceOf #0 is understood: it shares the participant with `transferFrom`, so its event is the
participant's *in-block* slot, and `getExternalCallReturnEventOutputIndex(0)` looks up
`external-call:<logicalReturnGroupIndex(...)>` in the tail list, which cannot find an event published under another
candidate's identity (`external-call:1:0`). The correct coordinate for `Idx0` is therefore **13 - the same output as
`transferFrom`** (which also explains why one commitment must satisfy both calls: `abi.encode(true)` = `..01` decodes as
`true` for the bool and as `1` for the uint256, both harmless/expected).

### The fix is now two concrete parts

1. **values**: re-apply the round-208 fabrication so the participant's return event carries `..01` instead of the
   one-byte fallback - without it, the seed publishes `00` for every candidate (round 209);
2. **witnesses**: write each returning call's witness from the *physical* coordinate of the event that call's
   participant publishes, i.e. resolve shared participants to their owner and use that owner's
   `getExternalCallReturnEventOutputIndex` - `Idx0` and `Idx1` both become **13**, `Idx2` becomes **7**. The current
   block (`dadd491bc`'s retarget) prefers the builder's answer only when it is >= 0 and otherwise keeps the stale plan
   value, which is exactly how `14`/`0`/`0` survived; the plan fallback must not be used for a coordinate that the
   builder has already placed.

## SESSION ROUNDS 211-241 -- return witnesses, block shape, entry coordinate (commit `afac71580`)

Baseline at session start: 29 passed / 37 failed; `take job` failed at probe `ip 309` (SafeERC20 catch path).
Now: same green set (fixture, `unicrow params` 2, `admin` 8, `register user` 2 all re-verified), and `take job`
reaches **`ip 6` of an 8-instruction outlined helper** - a *later* stage than any previous round.

### Four general fixes, all committed in `afac71580`

1. **Callee return values in probe builds** (`StatefulContract._createBuilder`, the direct `externalCallUtxoGroups.push`
   site). A return probe evaluates only the contract input, so a callee's covenant never runs and its return event
   keeps the neutral placeholder the builder seeds (`new Uint8Array([0])`). A caller decoding `bool` reads that as
   failure and takes its library's catch path (that was `ip 309`). Fabricated exactly like the nested path:
   `callee._deriveReturnValue(name, args)` + `encodeExternalReturnValue`, falling back to a literal `true` for a
   single-`bool` result (the compiler's convention for a state-writing callee). **Gated on
   `overrides?.returnProbeOnly === true`** - a broadcast transaction executes its callees and must not precompute.
   Measured: `balanceOf -> 00..00` (32 B), `transferFrom -> 00..01` (32 B).
2. **Return witnesses follow the assembled transaction.** `StatefulContract` now registers
   `builder._setMasterUnlockerRefresher(...)` whenever the top-level ABI has `__internal__externalReturnOutputIdxN`
   params; the refresher calls `refreshTopLevelReturnWitnesses(materialized)`, which re-reads
   `builder.getBuiltExternalCallReturnEventOutputIndex(groupIdx)` (then
   `getExternalCallReturnEventOutputIndex`) and rewrites those args before the unlocker is rebuilt. `topLevelReturnWitnessGroups`
   (pushed alongside `topLevelReturnWitnessPlan`) keeps witness ordinal -> group alignment. Also fixed
   `getExternalCallReturnEventOutputIndex` to read the *physical* group's `blockLayout` for the in-block return slot
   (an alias owns no layout, so it used to report -1). Final probe internals now name the outputs that actually carry
   the events: `__internal__externalReturnOutputIdx0/1/2 = 19/8/20` (balanceOf/transferFrom/balanceOf).
3. **Shared physical block adopts the denser writer shape** (`StatefulContract`, right after the direct group push).
   Several callsites can claim one callee master (a view first, then the writer). They share ONE physical block and
   the caller verifies the writer's callsite against the writer's own ABI layout, so when the new callsite's layout has
   more slots than the physical owner's, the owner takes `blockInputs`/`blockLayout`/`dataNftUtxos`/
   `requiredNftIndices`/`returnEventInBlock`. Without it: a `balanceOf` view block (master@0/entry@1/returnEvent@2,
   3 inputs) carried the writer's 8-slot batch plan, and derivation died in
   `Planned nested entry insert has no block input` (that throw now names both geometries).
4. **Batch lanes that read one predecessor.** A sorted-batch lane READS its predecessor UTXO; two lanes whose keys
   bracket the same entry name the same UTXO (an update of that entry + an insert whose predecessor it is). Keep the
   first occurrence as the block input, back the remaining slots with funders (layout width preserved), and rewrite
   that lane's `__internal__vmapBatchProof_N` to the surviving slot. Without it:
   `Duplicate stateful input <outpoint> ... roles external:0:block:2,external:0:block:4`.

Plus: entries are now emitted at the offset their declared block-layout slot publishes
(`StatefulTransactionBuilder`, `layoutEntrySlots` no longer requires `preserveBlockLayoutWidth`). Appending in slot
order only agrees while nothing else occupies the band; with value chunks / participants present the entry landed at
20 while the covenant read slot 4.

### Round 253: what the failing helper actually is (compiler side)

`GenerateTargetTraversal.ts:32155` `emitPickTrackedFromBottom(name)` emits exactly `OP_DEPTH; <n>; OP_SUB; OP_PICK` -
copy a tracked frame value (a **witness**) by its stable distance from the bottom. The failing 8-instruction helper is
that sequence continued by `OP_INPUTINDEX; OP_ADD; OP_UTXOBYTECODE; OP_EQUALVERIFY` (`OP_DROP; OP_DEPTH` is the
invoked-helper epilogue), i.e. it means:

    verify input[activeInputIndex + <witness>].lockingBytecode == <compiled constant>

So the operand that is wrong is the **witness value** the helper picked (7), not a compiled constant and not an
addressing mode: 7 must be the block offset of an INPUT that carries the expected address. The expected constant is
the Unicrow `escrows` entry address, whose input in this probe sits at block offset 4 (`__internal__vmapBatchProof_0
= 4`), while 7 is FakeToken's promoted `returnEvent@7` and equals `__internal__vmapBatchPredOut_0 = 7` (an **output**
coordinate). Pay's own block is only 7 slots wide (`master@0, dataNft@1-3, entry@4, event@5, returnEvent@6`), so an
input coordinate of 7 cannot exist in pay's block at all.

All `__internal__vmapBatch*` args are filled **by name** in the SDK (`bCompilerInternalArgs[..._${slotIndex}]`,
`lateInternalArgs`, `childCompilerInternalArgs`), so no ordinal/ordering bug is involved; either the compiled body
reads the PredOut witness where it needs the Proof witness, or the SDK published a PredOut value into a slot the body
reads as an input coordinate.

Cheapest confirmation (no code change): run `SOLIDC_DEBUG_DERIVE_TRACE_OPS=1 SOLIDC_DEBUG_SPAN_INSTRUCTIONS=8` and
read the span state at `ip: 2` (`OP_INPUTINDEX`) - `top` then holds the picked witness right below the active input
index. Correlate that value with the probe internals (`vmapBatchProof_*`, `vmapBatchPredOut_*`,
`extcallMasterIdx*`, `externalCallInputBase`) to name the exact parameter, then compare it with the artifact's ABI
parameter order for the call that owns the check.

### Round 256: the failing check borrows the CALLER's witness for a CALLEE coordinate

`SOLIDC_DEBUG_COMPUTE_BASE=1` produced no `DBG-COMPUTE-BASE` output because the marketplace artifacts are **prebuilt**

    <emitPickTrackedFromBottom(W)>            -> OP_DEPTH; len-index; OP_SUB; OP_PICK   (picked W, measured depth 3,
    <emitMasterInputIndex(...) plain branch>  -> OP_INPUTINDEX                          value 4)

and `emitSlotMasterIndex` (`:2337`) documents the designed alternative: "Prefers the SDK-filled per-slot runtime index

interface) shifted the fixed block offset."

So the check computes `input[OP_INPUTINDEX + W]` - the coordinate the *caller's* active input plus the *caller's*
tracked proof/`externalCallInputBase` witness (W = 4, which is exactly pay's `vmapBatchProof_0`) - while the constant
it authenticates is a **FakeToken**-band resource (at input 7 = FakeToken master 6 + 1). The callee's own check was
inlined into the caller's script but resolves its coordinate from the caller's ABI witnesses instead of the callee's
master (`__internal__extcallMasterIdx<slot>` = 6, now correctly bound by the round-243 fix).

**Concrete fix candidate:** make the emitter that produced `PICK; OP_INPUTINDEX; OP_ADD` for a callee-block coordinate

the green set before the ladder, since that comment also records that the two addressing forms trade regressions
(`close job` x2, `withdraw collateral`).

### Round 258: ROOT CAUSE - the callee identity check falls back to a caller-relative base inside an outlined span

The failing check is the external-call **target identity** check (`GenerateTargetTraversal.ts` ~30800):

    // 1. IDENTITY (ALL modes): B's master locking bytecode == the expected address.
    this.emit(Op.OP_UTXOBYTECODE);                 // [B_master_inputIdx, B_master_bytecode]
    ... addrName ? this.emitPickTrackedFromBottom(addrName) : push(addressLiteral) ...
    this.emitPreferLockingBytecode(); this.emit(Op.OP_EQUALVERIFY);

The expected address comes from the declared call target (the measured constant is the FakeToken address - the
DESIGNED behaviour), and the input index is emitted immediately before by `emitSlotMasterIndex(slot)` (`:30783`),
whose contract is documented at `:2337`:

    "Push a slot's callee master input index. Prefers the SDK-filled per-slot runtime index param
     (__internal__extcallMasterIdx<slotIndex> ...) so the covenant reads the RIGHT co-spent callee even when a
     prior callee's data-NFT count ... shifted the fixed block offset. Falls back to the compile-time
     externalCallInputBase + computedOffset for single-call slots without the param."

Measured: the check read input **4** = `__internal__externalCallInputBase` (+ 0), i.e. the **fallback** branch fired -
`getStackIndex('__internal__extcallMasterIdx<slot>', true) < 0` at emission time. Pay's ABI *does* carry
`__internal__extcallMasterIdx0..3` (the SDK fills them: 6/6/6/16 after the round-243 fix), so the parameter exists in
the function frame but is **not visible inside the outlined 875-instruction span** that contains this check. An
outlined/OP_INVOKE'd body tracks only its own parameters, so the per-slot master index is unavailable there and the
emitter silently degrades to the caller-relative compile-time base - which is exactly why the compiler's own comment
at `:32385` says the two addressing forms "compensate for OPPOSITE frame mismatches" and that a fix must correct the
MODEL, not the addressing form.

Fix direction (matches an existing pattern in the same file): thread the per-slot master index into the outlined span
the way compute/keccak side-cars already thread their block base
(`emitComputeSidecarBlockBase(loc, capturedName)` + `OUTLINED_COMPUTE_BLOCK_BASE`, `:32436+`), or mark such spans as
context-carrying so `emitSlotMasterIndex` keeps its preferred branch inside them. A cheaper interim: make
`emitSlotMasterIndex` throw (or record a requires() entry) instead of silently falling back when the function HAS the
per-slot parameter but the current traversal is an outlined body - that converts a silent wrong-coordinate into a
loud compile error and names every affected call site.

"Data NFT outputs at block layout deploy offset"). Neither is an input-bytecode check. The failing check therefore

a caller parameter (`emitPickTrackedFromBottom(addrName)` in the identity check).

Two readings remain, and one cheap log separates them:

   address belongs - note no currently-green marketplace title performs an external call into a stateful callee, so

2. the check is a **callee-side data-NFT identity/preservation** verification the compiler emits into the caller's span
   and it pushes the data-NFT lock on purpose - in which case only the coordinate (base + witness family) is wrong,
   as established in rounds 266-268.

Decisive measurement: log, in the SDK's external-call construction, the address it resolves for each call target
(interface -> registered deployment -> address/locking bytecode) next to `inner.address` and
`getDataNftLockingBytecode(categoryId)`. If any call target equals the data-NFT lock `aa204320cb008c0e6ed41abf...`,
reading 1 is confirmed and the fix is in target resolution; otherwise reading 2 holds and the fix is the coordinate
model (round 267/268). The same env-gated logging style as `SOLIDC_DEBUG_ENTRY_ADDR` applies.

### Round 274: the plan, the compiler and the assembled frame disagree about input ORDER

The SDK's own plan-time base for the caller's frame is

5 funder, 6 FakeToken master, 7 the external read data NFT (`aa204320...`, the expected lock), 8-9 FakeToken
resources, 16 the arbitrator master, 21-23 the contracts' own-address resources. So the caller's own ENTRY input has
been materialized BEFORE the read-only data NFT, pushing the read NFT from the planned 4 to the actual 7.

       const rebaseDynamicChunkForFrame = (inputs: readonly { txid: string; vout: number }[]): boolean => {
         const position = topLevelDynamicChunkArgumentIndex;
         if (position < 0 || firstRootDynamicChunk === undefined) return false;
         const current = finalArgs[position];

           === firstRootDynamicChunk.txid.toLowerCase() && input.vout === firstRootDynamicChunk.vout);

         finalArgs[position] = BigInt(localIndex);

Round 292: the `pay` probe's missing event was a FUNDER-PLAN shortfall, not a derivation gap

The ip-1147 window (`OP_PICK OP_INPUTINDEX OP_5 OP_ADD OP_OUTPUTTOKENCOMMITMENT OP_EQUALVERIFY`) verifies
`outputs[OP_INPUTINDEX + 5]` - slot 5 of the `pay` frame is `event#0`, and the probe carried a token-free P2PKH
funder there. Instrumented (`SOLIDC_DEBUG_EVENT_STAGE=1`, kept as a diagnostic) at the event stage of
`_deriveFullTransactionState`:

    balanced-positioned-inputs { blockSize: 7,
      missing: [ { offset: 6, slot: { kind: 'returnEvent', offset: 6 } } ],
      fundersProvided: 2, fundersRemaining: 0,
      trailingInputs: { loopAlignmentFunders: 1, total: 1 } }
    balanced-input-return-parts { positioned: 7, result: 6 }        <- slot 6 compacted away
    input-order-guard { blockSize: 7, funders: 2, hasExternalGroups: true, externalCallInputs: 14 }

So the dense (position-indexed) placement DID run with two funders, but `_buildInputs` splices the loop-alignment
funders out of the pool BEFORE it walks the block slots, leaving one funder for the frame's two output-only slots
(event@5, returnEvent@6). Slot 6 was compacted, `result.length` became 6, and `postBlockParticipants` (the
FakeToken callee block) started at index 6 - inside the caller's own block. Measured consequence in the same run:
`event-materialize { blockSize: 7, cursor: 20, eventSlots: [{ kind: 'event', offset: 5, slotIndex: 0 }] }` - the
event output was appended at 20 instead of 5.

Root cause: the funder plan (`StatefulContract._createBuilder`, the `trailingCapacity === 0` branch) counted only
the block's output-only slots. A block that publishes NO trailing capacity still materializes its runtime journal /
value-write records AFTER the complete fixed block (`plannedDynamicBand: { start: 18, end: 18, nNew: 1 }` for this
`pay` probe), and each record is an output that owes a paired input. Fixed by adding
`max(predictedDynamicBand.nNew, bandWidth)` to `neededFunders` when `trailingCapacity === 0`.

Round 293: event outputs must be placed at their slot offset, and a kernel route must reserve them at all

Two more general defects behind the same window:

* `StatefulTransactionBuilder.build()` appended every event output at the build cursor. That equals the published
  offset only when nothing but the owner's block was materialized before the loop; a nested participant block, a
  funding pad (`_padOutputsToIndex` mirrors the callee master's input coordinate) or a derived chunk leaves the
  cursor past it, so the slot kept its neutral pad and the event check could never pass. Event outputs are now
  placed at `blockLayout.slots[event].offset` (`assignBalancedOutputAtOffset`, padding with neutral `0x51` pads),
  displacing only a TOKENLESS occupant; an authenticated resource at the offset is left alone and the event is
  appended (the mismatch then stays the covenant's to refuse).
* A kernel route publishes no emits of its own - its handlers are the emitters - so `emitInfos` was empty for the
  route frame and no event placeholder existed at all. The selected rows' emits are now collected at
  `rowIndex * eventWidth + emitIndex` (`SOLIDC_DEBUG_EMIT_SOURCES=1` shows the union).

Round 294: SEC-11 own-category immutable pin vs. the platform's own return carriers (compiler change)

With the two SDK fixes the `pay` probe derives (the return blob is found) and the failure moves into
`send()`'s composed preflight:

    messageBus: BCH-2026 preflight failed at input 15 (ip 484 of 496, window 1:b8 138 99 2:6d81 138 84 85 165 105 104)
    failing opcode 105 (OP_VERIFY)

That window is `push(0xb8) OP_INVOKE OP_IF push(0x816d) OP_INVOKE push4 push5 OP_WITHIN OP_VERIFY` inside the
compiler's `emitOwnCategoryImmutableNftOutputPin` (GenerateTargetTraversal.ts, SEC-11): every own-category
immutable NFT must sit at an event slot offset, a witnessed return index, or carry the `SCID` envelope.
`SOLIDC_DEBUG_RETURN_LAYOUT=1` names the offenders:

    built: [ [external-call:0:0, 44], [external-call:1:0, 45], [external-call:4:0, 46], [external-call:7:0, 47],
             [external-call:3:0, 27], [external-call:5, 35] ]
    outputs 43-47: lock=51, capability none, 32-byte commitment   <- the caller's cross-call return carriers

`takeJob`'s own ABI names them (`externalReturnOutputIdx*`), but the callee frames cannot: the `publishJobEvent`
impl frame pins the PROXY's category (ee643a16) and the FakeToken participant pins its own category, and BOTH see
siblings' carriers. A carrier is necessarily an own-category immutable with `capability none` (the caller verifies
`retcat == callee master category`, capability `none`, FT amount 0, lock `OP_TRUE`), so no placement or category
choice can avoid the collision.

Resolution: the pin now excludes OP_TRUE-locked outputs from the *serialized event candidate* class. A log is read
back at its EVENT NFT COVENANT ADDRESS (`getEventNftAddress(category, signature)` -> a P2SH script hash, never the
single-opcode OP_TRUE lock), which is exactly what the pin protects; every addressable own-category immutable stays
refused. Measured: the composed preflight advances past input 15.

the caller identity belongs. Verified by the fact that the value never appeared anywhere in `finalArgs` under its
own ABI name while `derive-return-value-entry` showed the override arriving.

this session's measurements before it was found: the runs after editing `LowerCollectionJournalHelpers.ts` /
`LowerDynamicStateJournalHelpers.ts` reused cached artifacts (the only run that behaved differently was the one
whose *incidental* edit to `compiler.ts` changed the id). The id now folds the file count, total size and newest
mtime of every emitted module, and `SOLIDC_DEBUG_CACHE_ID=1` prints it. Verified: touching a nested pass module
changes the printed id; the full marketplace compile recompiles 22/22 sources.

**Where takeJob's two extra clone parameters come from (measured).** `LowerCollectionJournalHelpers` turns selected
internal helpers into journal handlers with
`parameters.unshift(...dynamicEntries, ...entries)` (`:504`) - one parameter per journalled dynamic array and per
journalled entry collection. For `MarketplaceV1.takeJob` those are exactly the missing
`(JobPost[], bool, ...)`: `jobs` is `JobPost[] public jobs` (the dynamic array) and `whitelistWorkers` is a
`mapping(uint256 => mapping(address => bool))` (bool entries). `LowerDynamicStateJournalHelpers:121` unshifts one
more (`valueType` of the dynamic state) - the same class of rewrite.

**Three guards were tried and all fail**, which is itself the useful result:
1. name-prefix skip of every `__message_bus_*` clone in both journal passes -> `Unicrow.sol` fails to compile:

   `synthesizeBatchBeforeLowering` call site) and skipping those -> `Unicrow.sol` fails identically.
So the journal lowering is REQUIRED for these clones even when the route text was generated first. Skipping it is
not an option; the generated route's call site must instead end up carrying the journal parameters - i.e. either
the pass's "Rewrite call sites before changing arities" step (`LowerCollectionJournalHelpers.ts:455`) must reach
the generated route's call node, or the route must be synthesized after this lowering for the kernel path.

Round 341 (goal round 341): the compiler defect behind `takeJob` is FIXED; `take job` now fails in the composer's
deferred-compute learning instead

**The fix (commit `2679e88fd`).** `LowerCollectionJournalHelpers` refused to rewrite a call inside a body whose
array had an unthreaded writer, but still unshifted the journal parameter and rewrote the candidate's own body -
so the callee declared a parameter no call site passed and its body referenced journal locals nothing declared.
Both halves are now consistent: a candidate is unshifted only when a rewritten call site actually threads it
(`threadedSingles`/`threadedMultis`), and a candidate's own body is rewritten only when it is journaled (callers
first, candidate bodies second - the codegen error for the other order was
`Undefined reference to symbol __dcj___message_bus_entry_takeJob_0`).

**Measured effect (forced full compile, 22/22 sources, EXIT 0):** `MarketplaceV1` 36 -> 39 eligible handlers;
`takeJob`, `refund` and `refuseArbitration` all generate routes now. `take job` therefore takes the ATOMIC path:
the composer batches the token's rows with per-row callers, so the missing `approve` write of round 353 is no
longer the failure.

**New failure, now precisely quantified** (commit `42f3476d4` prints it):

    Error: messageBus: complete graph did not expose arguments for all deferred compute resources
      (participant 0: keccak 2/2 unresolved, ecrecover 1/1 unresolved)

i.e. the `takeJob` row needs 2 keccak side-cars plus 1 ecrecover side-car, and the SDK's trace learners never
learned their arguments. Context measured with `SOLIDC_DEBUG_ECRECOVER_READINESS=1`:

* participant 0 is the delegate/proxy frame (`executionInput` 129, `inputBase` 0) with compute offsets [3,4,5]
  (3 = keccak mode 1, 4 and 5 = ecrecover mode 2), and the callManifest DOES carry kind-6 rows for 3, 4 and 5 -
  so the graph side is complete and only the *values* are missing;
* its route `__message_bus1` publishes no ecrecover/keccak arguments at all
  (`routedUnlockers[localIndex 129] -> arguments: []`);
* `MarketplaceV1`'s handler metadata for `takeJob` is `keccakPreimageParams: [null, null]`,
  `ecrecoverCompute: true`, and `ecrecoverArgParams` **absent** - the handler computes both the digest
  (`ECDSA.recover(digest, signature_)`, digest = keccak over `abi.encode(eventsLength, jobId_)`) and v/r/s from
  `signature_`, and codegen records arg provenance on the function that emits the call (`emitEcrecoverComputeCall`
  pushes into `this.currentFunction`), so a transitively inlined call leaves the entry point with
  `ecrecoverCompute: true` and no arg list.

otherwise) is the honest form. Measured for the failing participant:

cannot be an owner-based `entry` read picking up a wrong owner value.

the same numeric offset in an IMPLEMENTATION-relative layout is a different slot family - and
`GenerateTargetTraversal.ts:1998` deliberately builds `keccakSideCar`, `ecrecoverSideCar`, `transfer`, `tcTransfer`,
`event` and `returnEvent` on `OP_INPUTINDEX` (the executor) while everything else (including `entry` and `state`) uses
the owner. So the next measurement is to resolve the aborting instruction of the UNOPTIMISED probe against the

deliberately implementation-relative families and the defect is the *value* that family was given (or the ordering
of the trailing band), not the owner plumbing.

Round 350: the owner pick is an ABSOLUTE stack-bottom ordinal, and the frame is not at the bottom

**The compiler's own model, printed.** `emitPickTrackedFromBottom` now records every site under the existing
`SOLIDC_DEBUG_COMPUTE_BASE=1` gate as `DBG-BOTTOM-PICK` (function, name, topIndex, modelLength, ordinal+1,
outputLength, model neighbours). Recompiling the marketplace project with the gate (cache moved aside - solidhat's
project cache ignores the build id) shows the takeJob entry body's bottom picks ALL name
`__internal__messageBusOwnerInput` and all carry the same ordinal (`bottomOrdinalPlusOne = 15`), i.e. the compiler
reads the owner parameter at a fixed ABSOLUTE bottom ordinal (14) of its model:

    stackTop (model, top-down, site 0): eventsLength, __dlcache_jobs, __rh85_target, __rh83_target,
      __extaddr_unicrowAddress_IUnicrow, __extaddr_ll_jobs_jobId__token, __extaddr_marketplaceData,
      __extcap_4..0, jobId_, signature_, ek_key_0, ek_key_1, logical_caller, __internal__messageBusOwnerInput,
      __internal__dynamicChunkInputBase, __internal__outlinedRecoveryAIndex, ...
    modelLength 32, topIndex 17 -> bottom ordinal 14

`emitPickTrackedFromBottom` emits `OP_DEPTH; (modelLength - topIndex); OP_SUB; OP_PICK`, which resolves to the item
at bottom ordinal `modelLength - topIndex - 1` - correct only when the runtime stack bottom IS the frame's bottom.

**Measured runtime, same instruction (ip 226-229 of `__message_bus_entry_takeJob`, byte 292).** The picked item is
131 (`2:8300`) at bottom ordinal 14 while p0's band supplies `__internal__proxyMasterIndex = 0` (independent
`participant-witness-band` dump) and a one-byte 0 sits at bottom ordinal 19. So the runtime holds ~5 more items
BELOW the modelled frame than the model knows: the caller keeps live operands under the callee's argument band
(OP_INVOKE shares the stack). Together with the earlier finding that the top-relative form instead popped a 32-byte
entry commitment, the frame is sandwiched: caller operands BELOW, runtime-only operands ABOVE. Absolute-bottom
addressing cannot be right in that situation, and neither can a plain top-relative pick.

**Owner sentinel, per participant now.** `SOLIDC_DEBUG_OWNER_SENTINEL=1` substitutes `0x11 + participant` for
`__internal__proxyMasterIndex` (was a single 0x99 for every delegate, which cannot distinguish "another
participant's owner" from "a neighbouring witness"). Effect is unchanged and reproducible: with the sentinel the
deferred-compute learning COMPLETES, and preflight at input 129 then fails one step later, in a 23-instruction body
(`ip 3 of 23, failing opcode 127 (OP_SPLIT), window 206 1 ...` - a token-category read split on an EMPTY value).
That is the same failure class (a coordinate pointing at an unmaterialized slot) and is the next reachable blocker.

**Fix direction (general, compiler-side, no app-specific naming).** Parameter addressing must not depend on what the
caller leaves below the frame:
  (a) materialize `__internal__messageBusOwnerInput` (and the other hidden parameters) into a TRACKED LOCAL at body
      entry - at entry the callee's arguments are the last items the caller pushed, so a top-relative pick is exact
      there - and address that local afterwards; or
  (b) make the generated call sites invoke handler bodies with a cleaned stack (stash the caller's live operands in
      the alt stack across the OP_INVOKE); or
  (c) stop the SDK dispatcher from leaving operands under the callee's band.
(a) is compiler-only and is the smallest change that is sound for both sandwiched directions.

Greens/practicals: the compiler edit is diagnostic-only (gated print), the sentinel gate is debug-only; the
marketplace artifacts stay in the optimised state (same bytecode; the last compile only added debug records).

Round 350b: BOTH addressing forms fail, so the owner must be ANCHORED

A new mirror gate `SOLIDC_DEBUG_OWNER_TOP_HANDLER=<substring>` forces the compact top-relative form for a named
handler (the existing `SOLIDC_DEBUG_OWNER_BOTTOM_HANDLER` forces the bottom form). Recompiling the marketplace
project with `SOLIDC_DEBUG_OWNER_TOP_HANDLER=__message_bus_entry_takeJob` and running the title gives the SAME
stall (`keccak 2/2 unresolved, ecrecover 1/1 unresolved`, 472-input probe). So:

    bottom ordinal  -> picked 131 (a runtime item ~5 below the owner's real slot)
    top-relative    -> picks a different wrong item (the earlier measured 32-byte commitment)
    sentinel owner  -> learning completes, preflight fails later on an empty token-category split

Both forms address the owner POSITIONALLY, and the frame is sandwiched: caller operands below the argument band
(the model's absolute bottom is not the frame's) and runtime-only operands above it (the model's top index is not
the frame's top). No positional form can be right for such a frame.

Next round's fix (general, compiler-side): anchor the hidden owner parameter by VALUE instead of by position.
At body entry the callee's arguments are the last items the caller pushed, so a top-relative pick AT ENTRY is
exact; the value must then live somewhere that does not drift. Two candidates:

  (a) alt-stack anchor: at entry, materialize the owner (top-relative pick) and `OP_TOALTSTACK`; every later use
      becomes `OP_FROMALTSTACK OP_DUP OP_TOALTSTACK` (non-destructive read). Must first verify whether an OP_INVOKE
      made by the body gives the callee a fresh alt stack - if it does not, nested calls can interleave with it,
      so each nested call site must stash/restore its anchor (or the anchor must be moved to a fresh slot).
  (b) compute the frame bottom ONCE at entry (`OP_DEPTH; <parameterCount>; OP_SUB`) and keep it in the model as a
      named local, then emit picks as `OP_DEPTH; OP_SWAP/SUB`-style frame-relative reads. This only works if the
      model's count of the body's own pushes is exact, which the measured drift (~28 items above the owner) says it
      currently is NOT - so (b) needs the model fixed first, while (a) does not care about the drift at all.

Recommended order: implement (a) for `emitMasterInputIndex`'s owner branch only (takeJob's handler), measure the
title and the two currently green titles that depend on the compact form (`close job` both variants, `withdraw
collateral`), then widen if it holds.

Tooling added this round (all gated, no production behaviour change): `DBG-BOTTOM-PICK` (every bottom pick with its
model view, printed under `SOLIDC_DEBUG_COMPUTE_BASE=1` at COMPILE time), `SOLIDC_DEBUG_OWNER_TOP_HANDLER`, and the
per-participant `SOLIDC_DEBUG_OWNER_SENTINEL` (0x11 + participant). Reminder: `DBG-*` offsets are pre-assembly, so
they cannot be aligned with shipped body offsets - select by function name + ordinal + name, not by offset.

entry keys, then the source args - i.e. the caller pushes the argument vector in declaration order, exactly as the

(`SOLIDC_DEBUG_OWNER_TOP_HANDLER`) leaves the title stalling.

Round 351b: the model's PARAMETER ORDER is right - the count BELOW it is wrong

Reading the seeding mechanics settles the direction of the error:

  * `pushToStack(value, pushToBottom)` -> `stack.push` for `true`, `stack.unshift` otherwise, and `getStackIndex`
    is a raw `indexOf`, so index 0 is the TOP of the model.
  * `visitParameter` seeds every parameter with `pushToBottom = true`, i.e. declaration order appended DOWNWARD:
    the model's order is [.., jobId_, signature_, key0, key1, logical_caller, owner] from the top, so the owner is
    the DEEPEST declared parameter and `jobId_` sits six slots above it.
  * The measured entry stack agrees exactly: pre-body top-down = [0 (owner), 65-byte signature_, 0 (jobId_),
    25-byte P2PKH (key1 = msg.sender)], i.e. the caller pushes the vector in REVERSE declaration order and the
    model's parameter layout matches it one for one. `message-bus-clone-params` + `message-bus-arg-order` also
    agree index for index (owner parameter fed from `__internal__proxyMasterIndex` = 0 for participant 0).

So the layout is right and only the DEPTH BELOW the picked value is wrong: at the failing pick the model reports the
owner at bottom ordinal 14, while the runtime measurement puts it at depth 71 of a 90-item stack, i.e. **19 items
below it** - a discrepancy of exactly 5. The model's bottom region is seeded with synthetic entries
(`visitParameter` bottom pushes plus `pushToStack(name, true)` for outlined bases, `constructorCaptures`,
`OUTLINED_TRAILING_BASE` / `OUTLINED_COMPUTE_BLOCK_BASE` / `OUTLINED_RECOVERY_A_INDEX`) and the runtime frame has
the route band plus the batch copy instead - so the bottom-relative ordinal addresses a NEIGHBOURING route witness
(`graphFixedSize`/`graphBlockSize` = 131 in this frame) rather than the parameter. That is the whole failure.

`DBG-BOTTOM-PICK` now also prints `stackBottom` (the last 14 model entries) so the next run NAMES the model's
bottom items and shows which of them the runtime never pushes.

**Next round, first action**: recompile with `SOLIDC_DEBUG_COMPUTE_BASE=1` (move `.marketplace/cache` aside; the
project cache ignores the build id), take the `__message_bus_entry_takeJob` `DBG-BOTTOM-PICK` records and compare
`stackBottom` with the runtime frame: the fix is to seed the DEFINE'd route handler's frame model with the items the
caller actually leaves below the argument band (or to drop the synthetic entries the shipped body never pushes), so
the ordinal and the runtime agree. Then re-run the title and confirm the coordinate becomes 20 (participant 0's
entry slot 0) instead of 151, and re-run `close job` (both) + `withdraw collateral`.

Round 351c: the model's bottom region is handler-local, the runtime's is the caller's band

`DBG-BOTTOM-PICK.stackBottom` (last 14 model entries, deepest first) for every takeJob owner pick, identical at every
model length:

    __internal__dynamicChunkInputBase, __internal__outlinedRecoveryAIndex, __internal__handlerEffectSite,
    __internal__handlerStaticDirty, __internal__handlerStaticMode, __internal__graphEmissions,
    __internal__state_write_marketplaceData, __internal__state_write_jobs, __internal__dynwrite_value_jobs,
    __internal__state_write_unicrowAddress, __internal__state_write_treasuryAddress,
    __internal__state_write_unicrowMarketplaceFee, __internal__state_write_PausableStorage___paused,
    __internal__graphHandlerCallerDepth

and the owner sits immediately ABOVE that block (ordinal 14 = the block's size). So the model seeds the handler's
own pending-effect locals BELOW its parameters - items that, at runtime, the handler pushes later into its working
region (or never, on an inactive branch). The runtime's below-owner region is instead the CALLER's band copy:
measured depths 71-89 of the 90-item frame (ordinals 0-18) are `graphSettlementBoundary`, framed `graphCallers`,
997-byte `graphEmissions`, `graphFixedSize`, `graphBlockSize`, `activeVerifierIndex`, the batch blob, a framed lock
and the caller's own 0 - i.e. exactly the published route inputs, in descending index order, with the owner (0) on
top of them.

Consequences, all measured:
  * the model's frame (31-58 items) is far smaller than the runtime frame (90), so ~39 items the body pushes are
    untracked as well - positional addressing of ANY kind (bottom ordinal or top index) cannot be right for these
    DEFINE'd handler frames;
  * that is exactly why `SOLIDC_DEBUG_OWNER_TOP_HANDLER=__message_bus_entry_takeJob` changes nothing: the pick still
    addresses a position the runtime does not share;
  * the ordinal lands on `graphFixedSize`/`graphBlockSize` (131) - a caller band item - which the outlined entry
    check then turns into the coordinate `131 + 20 = 151` (participant 1's `returnEvent` slot, a filler input).

So the fix is confirmed to be VALUE anchoring rather than position: read the owner once at handler entry (it is the
TOP item there - measured pre-body top = empty item = 0 = participant 0's `__internal__proxyMasterIndex`) and keep
it in the alt stack for drift-free re-reads (`OP_FROMALTSTACK OP_DUP OP_TOALTSTACK`). OP_INVOKE shares both stacks
(`opInvoke` in libauth only swaps `instructions`/`ip` and pushes a control frame), so the anchor must be balanced
across nested invokes the body makes - the compiler's own alt use is already to/from balanced, which the takeJob
title will confirm.

Tooling state: `SOLIDC_DEBUG_COMPUTE_BASE=1` at COMPILE time now yields both DBG-COMPUTE-BASE and DBG-BOTTOM-PICK
(with `stackBottom`); the marketplace artifacts are rebuilt canonically afterwards.

  * the DEFINE'd body captures the owner into the ALT STACK at entry and every owner read becomes

  1. enumerate all call sites of the affected clones (`dispatchFor` sites and any direct handler invocation) and

Round 352b: prime suspect for "something after the owner"

The three titles that broke with the capture ON are exactly the ones whose handlers carry kernel-JOURNAL context: the

only when a rewritten call site actually threads it"), and those threaded operands are appended to the clone's

reads that witness instead of the owner - which is what the OP_UTXOBYTECODE failure at input 129 (ip 245 of 6337)
looks like.

So the next round's first measurement is: compile with `SOLIDC_DEBUG_ARG_ORDER=1` (move `.marketplace/cache` aside
first; the project cache ignores the build id) and diff, for each affected clone, `message-bus-clone-params` (the
clone's declared list after every injection) against `message-bus-arg-order` (the emitted vector) - the tail AFTER
`__internal__messageBusOwnerInput` is the thing to eliminate. `SOLIDC_DEBUG_ARG_ORDER` currently prints the clone
list at owner-append time, so extend it to print the FINAL list (after SymbolTableTraversal's injections) for a
precise diff.

**New instrument.** `SOLIDC_DEBUG_ARG_ORDER=1` now also prints `message-bus-define-params`: the clone's FINAL declared
parameter list (with the owner index) at emission time, i.e. after every injection. The old print
(`message-bus-clone-params`) runs when the owner is appended, before SymbolTableTraversal adds its witnesses, so it
could not show what sits after the owner.

**Audit result (all 43 route clones).** Every clone declares MORE parameters than its emitted call vector passes,
and ten of them have trailing parameters AFTER the owner:

    __message_bus_entry_takeJob        params 7, vector 6, tail [owner, __internal__dynamicChunkInputBase]
    __message_bus_entry_refund         params 7, vector 6, tail [owner, __internal__dynamicChunkInputBase]
    __message_bus_entry_pay            params 10, vector 7, tail [owner, __internal__valueWitness_0,
                                                                   __internal__leadingPushValue_0,

    ... same shape for challenge/settle/postThreadMessage/publishJobPost/updateJobWhitelist

Root cause of the short vector: `__internal__dynamicChunkInputBase` is injected by SymbolTableTraversal AFTER route
synthesis, so the dispatch sites cannot see it in the parameter list.

**Measured: "fixing" the arity is NOT the fix.** Two coordinated changes were tried and both were reverted:
  1. symbol table: splice the chunk base BEFORE the owner (owner stays last) - alone changes nothing;
  2. dispatch sites: pass `__internal__dynamicChunkInputBase` ahead of the owner (predicted from
     `usesDynamicChunkInputBase`).

`__internal__proxyMasterIndex`), and yet `close job` (both) and `withdraw collateral` - which pass on the reverted

every later operand. This is the strongest evidence yet that the DEFINE'd handler ABI is positional-by-construction

body ends with the owner operand (or until the model is fixed).

Round 354: the alt-stack anchor leaks - diagnosed, and fixed at the call site

**The leak (found and explained).** The opt-in capture stores the owner on the ALT stack at body entry and
re-reads it non-destructively. Nothing drops it on the callee's exits, so every invocation leaked one alt item -
and the CALLER immediately runs alt-stack rotations of its own: `emitReplaceCompilerRouteFrameValue` (called right
after an internal `OP_INVOKE` to replace the caller-owned journal contexts) shuttles the intervening values through
the alt stack. Measured effect: with the capture on, `close job` (both) and `withdraw collateral` failed in ~100 ms
at ONE shared `OP_VERIFY` inside the `publishJobPost` entry body (`VM failed at ip 470 opcode 118`), because the
caller's rotation read the leaked item. That is why the capture "broke everything" even though the anchored reads
were correct in the bodies that captured properly.

Changes made this round (all dormant unless `SOLIDC_OWNER_ALT_ANCHOR=1`):
  * `ownerAnchorPreconditionHolds(env, node)` - ONE predicate used by both sides: the env gate, the callee declares
    `__internal__messageBusOwnerInput`, and route synthesis marked the owner as the call's LAST argument. Call sites
    use the same predicate to drop the leaked copy, so the two sides cannot disagree;
  * the flag is now per EMISSION (`visitFunctionDefinition` resets `messageBusOwnerAltAnchor = false`), because the
    same function is emitted as an entry body, as its OP_DEFINE body and as a subroutine-use probe;
  * the capture is back on the alt stack (drift-free) and every internal call site emits
    `OP_FROMALTSTACK OP_DROP` after the invoke when the callee anchors (the leak is dropped before the caller's own
    rotations);
  * route synthesis now derives the precondition from the EMITTED vector (`argumentVector.at(-1) ===
    routeOwnerInputExpression`) instead of from the presence of `ownerContextArgs` - the latter marked clones whose
    vector actually ends with another operand (measured: `publishJobPost` captured the dynamic-chunk base).

Measured with the capture on after those fixes: the shared `publishJobPost` require is GONE and the failure moved to
`ip 245 of 6337` (`OP_UTXOBYTECODE`, the implementation body) - i.e. the leak is closed but at least one anchored
body still captures a value that is not the owner (or one call site still misses the drop). Two suspects, both
checkable with existing tools: (a) a body whose vector ends with the owner but whose caller pushes runtime operands
AFTER the arguments (kernel journal threading), (b) an invoke path that is not the generic internal-call emitter
where the drop was added.

**Verified state (default configuration, gate off).** `close job` before/after timeout + `withdraw collateral`:
3 passed | 63 skipped. Fast fixture: 1 passed | 1 skipped. `take job`: deferred-compute stall (unchanged).

Round 354b: the anchor precondition (conjunction over all sites) is still not sufficient

Two further results, both measured with `SOLIDC_OWNER_ALT_ANCHOR=1`:

  * the leak fix works as intended: the shared `publishJobPost` require no longer fires, and the failure moves on;
  * the remaining failure is now IN an anchored body and its window shows the anchored read itself:
    `... 1:12 121 108 118 107 199 ...` = `push 18, OP_PICK, OP_FROMALTSTACK, OP_DUP, OP_TOALTSTACK,
    OP_UTXOBYTECODE` - i.e. the value the capture stored is not the owner for that body (input 129, ip 245 of a
    6337-instruction body, failing opcode 199);
  * making the precondition a CONJUNCTION over every emitted site (`messageBusOwnerIsLastArgument` ANDed at both
    dispatch sites) did not change that, so the multisite hole is not the remaining cause.

So at least one anchored body's entry top is not the owner even though its emitted vector ends with the owner
expression. The remaining explanations, in order of likelihood:
  1. the caller pushes runtime-only operands AFTER the argument vector (kernel-journal threading) - the same
     mechanism the arg-order audit could not see because those operands never appear in the generated call string;
  2. an OP_INVOKE path that is not the generic internal-call emitter (line ~11485) where the leak drop was added,
     so an earlier nested call leaks and shifts this body's alt stack;
  3. the alt stack already holds an item when the body starts (the route's own alt use), so the capture's item is
     not at the depth a later read assumes - the read is `OP_FROMALTSTACK` (top of alt) so this only matters if
     something pushes onto the alt stack between capture and read without popping.

Next round's cheapest discriminator: run the failing title with the capture on and the derive-op gate aimed at the
anchored body's first instructions (`FROM_IP=0 TO_IP=3`, `INSTRUCTION_COUNT` = the body's size, `STACK_DEPTH=0`):
if the entry top is the owner, explanation 1/3 holds; if it is another operand, the caller really does push

**Verified state (default, gate off)**: greens 3 passed | 63 skipped, fast fixture 1 passed | 1 skipped, `take job`

Round 355: the anchors are CONSISTENT now - all four titles fail at one shared outlined check

**The capture position was wrong, and now it is right.** Reading the call emitter settles the argument order:
`visitFunctionCall` pushes the vector with `for (let i = node.parameters.length - 1; i >= 0; i--)`, i.e. in
REVERSE - so argument k lands at depth k at entry, exactly the order `visitParameter` seeds the model in
(`pushToBottom` in declaration order, index 0 = top). Depth 0 therefore reads the FIRST argument, not the owner;
the model's index is the correct anchor. Measured confirmation: with the depth-0 capture, `publishJobPost`'s body
failed an OP_UTXOBYTECODE check whose window was literally my anchored read
(`1:12 121 108 118 107 199` = `push 18, OP_PICK, OP_FROMALTSTACK, OP_DUP, OP_TOALTSTACK, OP_UTXOBYTECODE`).

With `push <model index of owner>; OP_PICK; OP_TOALTSTACK` at entry (plus the call-site leak drop and the
per-emission flag), all four titles now fail at ONE shared defect instead of at anchor-related checks:

    input 129, `ip 3 of 6, failing opcode 127 (OP_SPLIT)`, window `121 124 127 124`,
    "stack item length: 36; requested split index: 116"

That 6-instruction body is `MarketplaceV1.invokeDebug[22]` (source span `marketplaceData.publishJobEvent(jobId_,
event_);`), i.e. the OUTLINED external-call target authentication. Its call sites (found by scanning every body for
`push 0x16; OP_INVOKE`) all have this shape:

    ... OP_PICK(121) OP_CAT(126) OP_DUP(118) push 0xf4 OP_INVOKE(138) push <n> push 0x16(22) OP_INVOKE(138)

and the outline itself is `OP_PICK OP_SWAP OP_SPLIT OP_SWAP OP_ROT OP_EQUALVERIFY`. The split index the VM reports
(116 = 0x74) is a SELECTOR byte, not a length, so the value the outline uses as an index is being read from the
wrong place - the same class of positional misread as the owner, now in the outlined target check.

**The real shape of the arity gap.** The call emitter pushes the argument vector in REVERSE (`for i =
params.length - 1; i >= 0; i--`), so the vector's LAST element is the DEEPEST frame item. A clone that declares
parameters the vector does not pass (the injected `__internal__dynamicChunkInputBase`, value witnesses, ...) is
therefore missing its DEEPEST slots, and every remaining parameter sits one depth shallower than the model says -
which is exactly the condition under which a top-relative model index picks a neighbouring item.

    that inserted the witness BEFORE the owner (which moved every existing depth and broke these titles);
