    which the caller band - not the parameter depths - breaks).

**Capture + tail fill**: the greens fail at the SAME shared 6-instruction outlined emission check as before
(`input 129, ip 3 of 6, window 121 124 127 124`), so the capture still perturbs that frame's inputs even when the
frame matches its declaration. New evidence on that check from the emitter (`GenerateTargetTraversal.ts` ~19168):
it computes `(__graph_prefix_length) = len(emission)` with `OP_DUP OP_SIZE OP_NIP`, picks `expected` by model index,
then `OP_SWAP OP_SPLIT OP_SWAP OP_ROT OP_EQUALVERIFY`. In the failing run the item split is 36 bytes while the
requested index is 116 - i.e. the split lands on the framed single-row value while the index came from the longer
vector. So the two operands at that OP_SPLIT are ordered for the *working* (positional) owner value and become
inconsistent when the owner is read correctly.

**Where that leaves the fix**: the working configuration relies on a positional read whose VALUE the rest of the
codegen is calibrated to; a correct owner value unmasks the ordering assumption in the outlined emission check. The
next round should therefore fix that outlined check (split the long vector at the prefix length, then compare the
peeled prefix against the short expected row) *before* promoting the capture - or, equivalently, verify which of the
two items that OP_SPLIT is supposed to consume by decoding the model (`pushToStack('(__graph_prefix_length)')` and
`pushToStack('(__graph_expected_emissions)')` are adjacent in the model, so the emitted order can be read off the

Round 357: the outlined emission check decoded - it is the same model/frame divergence

**The check, decoded.** `GenerateTargetTraversal.ts` ~19130-19180 builds the *actual* emission row
(target || selector || args, with `__graph_emission_row` / `__graph_prefix_length` tracked names) and then, when the
row has return values, emits exactly the 6 instructions that get outlined:

    OP_DUP OP_SIZE OP_NIP            -> prefix length of the row (model: (__graph_prefix_length))
    <push slot> OP_PICK              -> the authenticated emissions vector (model: (__graph_expected_emissions))
    OP_SWAP OP_SPLIT OP_SWAP OP_ROT OP_EQUALVERIFY
    (model: pop 3, push (__graph_result_frame))

Semantics per the code: split the EXPECTED emissions vector at the length of the constructed prefix, and compare the
peeled prefix with the constructed one. That is correct *provided the pick resolves to the emissions vector*. In the
capture+tail run it did not: the split item was 36 bytes (a framed 35-byte locking bytecode) while the requested
index was 116 (the full prefix length), i.e. the pick landed on a single-row value instead of the long vector.

**Why that matters: one root cause for both misreads.** The callee's frame model places the route's band witnesses
(`__internal__graphEmissions`, ...) in its BOTTOM region - the `DBG-BOTTOM-PICK.stackBottom` dump shows
`__internal__graphEmissions` among the last 14 model entries for the takeJob body - while the emitted call vector
does not pass them at all: at runtime they are the CALLER's band, sitting BELOW the argument band on the shared
stack. A top-relative read of such a name therefore uses a model index that does not describe the runtime depth
(measured: it fetched a 36-byte row instead of the vector), and a bottom-relative read is off by the difference
between the model's seeded bottom items and the caller's real band (measured earlier: it fetched
`graphFixedSize`/`graphBlockSize`). A correct handler frame model must seed the CALLER's band in its true order and
count, not the handler-local effect items, which the runtime pushes later (or never).

**Change landed this round**: the route ABI tail fill is now DEFAULT ON (`SOLIDC_ROUTE_ABI_TAIL=0` opts out). It is
verified safe - `close job` (both) + `withdraw collateral`: 3 passed | 63 skipped; fast fixture: 1 passed | 1 skipped
- and it removes a real defect (a clone whose declared tail the vector omits no longer leaves its deepest slots
unfilled). `take job` is unchanged (deferred-compute stall), as expected while its owner read still uses the
bottom-ordinal form.

**Next round**: seed the handler frame model with the caller's band (the route ABI inputs in the caller's push order,
so they land BELOW the parameter block) instead of the handler-local effect seeds, then measure with the capture on:
the outlined emission check's pick must resolve to the long vector (36 vs 116 disappears) and `close job` /
`withdraw collateral` must stay green.

Round 361: band-seeding the handler frame model - wired, but its source is not reachable there

**Why the band matters.** The runtime of a route handler is `[param 0 (top) ... param N-1, <caller band>, ...]`:
the call emitter evaluates the argument vector with `for (i = parameters.length - 1; i >= 0; i--)`, so the FIRST
parameter is pushed LAST and sits on top, while the caller's own frame - the route's ABI inputs (batch blob + 17
witnesses), which the SDK pushes in declared order - stays BELOW the arguments. The handler's frame model seeds
parameters (index 0 = shallowest = the first parameter, correct) but NOT the band, so a bottom-ordinal read of a band
value, or of the owner (whose ordinal is `modelLength - topIndex - 1`), addresses a neighbouring item. Measured
consequence: the takeJob owner pick returns `graphFixedSize`/`graphBlockSize` (131) instead of 0, turning the
intended entry coordinate 20 into 151.

**Implementation attempted (gated `SOLIDC_HANDLER_BAND_MODEL=1`).** Route synthesis stashes the route's parameter
names on every clone (`FunctionDefinitionNode.messageBusCallerBandNames`), and codegen appends them to the handler's
model AFTER the parameter block, skipping `batchBlob` - i.e. exactly the items that sit below the arguments, in the
order the runtime has them.

**Measured: the stash finds no route.** Under `SOLIDC_DEBUG_ARG_ORDER=1` the new `message-bus-caller-band` record
reports `routeFound: false` for every contract (e.g. `EACCToken ... clones 8`), so the seeds never apply and the
emitted owner ordinal is unchanged (the artifact still shows `OP_DEPTH; 15; OP_SUB; OP_PICK`). The route function is
not identifiable at that point in route synthesis - either it is created later, or it does not yet carry the
`batchBlob` parameter my predicate keys on.

**Next round**: find the point where the route's ABI inputs actually exist (the code that builds `route.inputs` for
the artifact, or the route function's construction) and stash the names there - then the ordinal should shift from
15 to 15+17 and the owner read should return 0, i.e. the coordinate 20, WITHOUT the alt-stack capture. That is the
fix the codegen comment itself demands ("must correct the MODEL ... not the addressing form").

**Verified state (defaults)**: greens 3 passed | 63 skipped; fast fixture 1 passed | 1 skipped; artifacts rebuilt
canonically; both `SOLIDC_HANDLER_BAND_MODEL` and `SOLIDC_OWNER_ALT_ANCHOR` remain opt-in.

Round 362: THE MODEL FIX CLEARS THE TAKE-JOB STALL - both paths now converge on the outlined check

**The band source is found.** The route's ABI inputs are built as a *parameter list* in `compiler.ts` (~9212,
`routeParameterList` -> `routeParameters`), which is AFTER the clone loop - that is why stashing the band at the
clone registry reported `routeFound:false`. Stashing the names where the list is actually built
(`FunctionDefinitionNode.messageBusCallerBandNames`) makes the seeding live: with
`SOLIDC_HANDLER_BAND_MODEL=1` the takeJob entry body changes shape (2408 -> 2390 instructions, many emitted pick
constants shift), i.e. the handler frame model now contains the caller's band below the argument block.

**Result: the deferred-compute stall is GONE.**

    before: "messageBus: complete graph did not expose arguments for all deferred compute resources
             (participant 0: keccak 2/2 unresolved, ecrecover 1/1 unresolved) [probe program: 472 inputs, ...]"
    after:  composition completes; preflight runs the real transaction and fails at
             input 129, `ip 3 of 6, failing opcode 127 (OP_SPLIT)`, window `121 124 127 124`

That is exactly the outlined emission check the alt-stack capture also reached, so both independent fixes - correct
the MODEL (band seeding) and capture the owner (alt-stack anchor) - converge on the SAME remaining defect. The stall
was a consequence of the wrong coordinate (151 instead of 20); with the model repaired the probe's entry check

**Regression status.** The band seeding is NOT yet safe as a default: with it on, `close job` (both) and
`withdraw collateral` fail at that same outlined check (they pass on the canonical build). So it stays opt-in, and
the outlined emission check is now THE single blocker to fix - it is the next defect on both paths, and fixing it
should let the model fix become the default and take `take job` past preflight.

**Verified state (defaults)**: greens 3 passed | 63 skipped; fast fixture 1 passed | 1 skipped; artifacts rebuilt
canonically; `SOLIDC_HANDLER_BAND_MODEL` and `SOLIDC_OWNER_ALT_ANCHOR` both opt-in.

Round 363: the handlers are invoked from NESTED bodies, so a fixed band seed cannot be sound

**Why the band seeding regresses the greens.** The failure dump's `controlStack` names the caller frames. For the
failing frames it is `[.., {ip:3159, instructionCount:11117}, {ip:321, instructionCount:6338}, {ip:2,
instructionCount:7}]` - i.e. the handler is invoked from large COMPILER-EMITTED bodies (6338 / 11117 instructions),
not from the route (which is a few hundred). So the operands physically below a handler's argument block are that
caller's own live locals, and the route ABI inputs are further down still. Seeding only the route band therefore
under-counts by an unbounded amount; measured symptoms after the seed:

  * band WITHOUT `batchBlob`: a 32-byte token category was compared against a 35-byte locking bytecode - an
    always-false comparison (off by exactly one, which is why the blob matters: the SDK pushes
    `[blob, ...routeWitnesses]`, so the blob is the deepest band item and must be seeded too);
  * band WITH `batchBlob`: the outline failure disappears and preflight instead fails at
    `input 129, ip 66 of 75, failing opcode 127 (OP_SPLIT)`, "stack item length: 31; requested split index: -32"
    - a negative index, i.e. a frame item read from the wrong slot again.

**Conclusion.** Any *fixed* band seed is unsound for these frames; the only sound model fix would be to seed the
caller's COMPLETE live stack, which the callee cannot know. That leaves the two value-anchored options already
identified: (a) capture the values a body needs at its entry, where depths are exact (the alt-stack anchor, opt-in
today), or (b) make the generated call sites invoke handler bodies with a cleaned stack, so the callee's frame really
does start at the stack bottom.

The band seeding stays opt-in (`SOLIDC_HANDLER_BAND_MODEL=1`) - it is still the change that CLEARS take-job's
deferred-compute stall, so it remains the useful bisect tool - and it must not become the default while it regresses
the three green titles.

Also improved this round: the preflight pre-state capture is keyed by input (`preStateByInput`), so a dump can no
longer show another input's frame. Caveat recorded: preflight may evaluate an input in several passes, so the
captured state is the last one seen for that input; the VM's own message remains the authority for the failing
operands.

**Verified state (defaults)**: greens 3 passed | 63 skipped; fast fixture 1 passed | 1 skipped; artifacts rebuilt
canonically; `SOLIDC_HANDLER_BAND_MODEL` and `SOLIDC_OWNER_ALT_ANCHOR` both opt-in.

Round 364: the two fixes have DIFFERENT next blockers; band+capture does not compose

**Measured matrix** (all with the title-level tests; canonical = both gates off):

    canonical          stall (take job)            greens PASS
    band model only    stall CLEARED               greens fail: outlined emission check
                                                    (input 129, ip 3 of 6, window 121 124 127 124)
    band + blob seed   stall CLEARED               greens fail: `EACCToken.invokeDebug[-40]`, a

    capture only       stall CLEARED               greens fail: the same outlined emission check

caller-aware for a shared body). The capture direction is the viable one, and its remaining blocker is a

row index (the composer builds the latter from the prepared call: `PreparedAtomicMessageBusCall.contract` /

Round 366: the failing split's operands come from the VM, and outlining is the prime suspect

The pre-state selector now prints EVERY candidate whose position matches the reported failure, because an outlined
body is invoked many times and preflight evaluates an input in several passes. Measured for the emission check:

    reported: input 129, ip 3, len 6, failing opcode 127 (OP_SPLIT)
    candidates whose (instructions.length, ip) match `evaluated.ip - 1`: 64
    VM message: "stack item length: 36; requested split index: 116"

The count is the point: position alone cannot identify the failing invocation, and the ring's last entry belongs to a
later pass (the report is emitted for the first failure while evaluation continues), so the dumped operands keep
disagreeing with the VM's own numbers. The VM message stays the authority, and it says exactly:

  * the split INDEX is 116 - the byte length of the emissions VECTOR (a computed size, not a byte string);
  * the split ITEM is 36 bytes - a framed 35-byte locking bytecode, i.e. a single row's target.

So the size was computed from the VECTOR while the item split is a ROW: the two values sit in the opposite order
from what the emitter assumes (it builds the row last, so the row should be on top and the vector below). The
caller's own sequence before the outline call (decoded from the artifact, `MarketplaceV1.invokeDebug[56]`, ip
5210-5229) is

    OP_INVOKE(0x80ae) OP_IF OP_INVOKE(0x80af) OP_NIP push 0x82 OP_INVOKE OP_NIP NIP NIP
    OP_SIZE OP_PICK OP_CAT OP_DUP push 0xf4 OP_INVOKE push 0x3e push 0x16 OP_INVOKE

i.e. the emitter's `OP_DUP OP_SIZE NIP` (its prefix-length step) is NOT contiguous with the `push idx; OP_PICK` that
follows it - other outlined helpers (0xf4 and the 0x80ae/0x80af pair) sit between them and around them. That is
consistent with the earlier bisect: with `SOLIDCASH_NO_OUTLINE=1` the emission check does NOT fail (the title then
fails somewhere else, `input 3, ip 4537 of 9343, OP_EQUALVERIFY`). So the outlining pass is the prime suspect: it
either placed the extracted boundary inside the row/prefix-length sequence or the extracted helper's own frame
expectation differs from the inline form.

**Next round**: compare the inline sequence the emitter writes for this check with the outlined decomposition for
one concrete call site (the helper ids 0xf4 / 0x80ae / 0x80af are all visible in the artifact, and
`SOLIDCASH_NO_OUTLINE=1` produces the inline reference), then fix whichever side lost the ordering - or make the
outline of THIS sequence preserve it. The VM message is the acceptance test: with the fix, the index must equal the
ROW PREFIX length (74) and the item must be the VECTOR (116 bytes).

Round 368: the post-job group addresses an UNMATERIALIZED output (154) - and the band model regresses here too

**The failing check, measured** (`post job 1`, canonical build,
`SOLIDC_DEBUG_FAILURE_POINT=1 SOLIDC_DEBUG_FAILURE_POINT_PRE_STATE=1 SOLIDC_TRACE_INPUT=216`):

    reported: input 216, ip 20589 of 22949, failing opcode 136 (OP_EQUALVERIFY)
    window:   push 0x82, INVOKE, NIP, push 0x5b81, INVOKE, OP_3, PICK, ADD, OP_2, PICK, ADD, DUP,
              OP_OUTPUTBYTECODE, INVOKE(0x2f), OP_15, INVOKE, INVOKE(0x33), INVOKE(0xeb), INVOKE(0xf5),
              EQUALVERIFY, DUP, push 0x1c
    pre-state (all 64 candidate executions agree, so these ARE the operands):
              d1 = 000100 (256), d0 = 9a00 (154)   <- the compared pair
              deeper: a 130-byte commitment-like blob, "DIGITAL_VIDEO", small ints
    tailIndexedOutput: { index: 154, lockingBytecode: "51", exactInputMatches: [] }

So the code computed the OUTPUT coordinate 154 (`OP_3 PICK ADD` then `OP_2 PICK ADD`, i.e. two frame reads
added), read `outputs[154].lockingBytecode`, and got the one-byte FILLER `51` (OP_1) - an unmaterialized slot -
with no input matching it either. The comparison then fails between 154 and 256. Same class as the take-job
coordinate: a coordinate computed from frame reads lands on a placeholder.

**The band model regresses this group as well.** With `SOLIDC_HANDLER_BAND_MODEL=1` all four titles of the group
(`post job 1`, `post two jobs`, `post job with whitelist`, `dispute > sanity checks no arbitrator`) fail EARLIER
(15-25 s instead of 75-106 s) at the same 75-instruction encoder helper the three green titles hit
(`input 129, ip 66 of 75, failing opcode 127`). That is the second independent group where the band model converts a
failure into the encoder failure, so it is confirmed unsafe as a default.
